blind.B1: Yes. All 25 subjects (14 ME/CFS, 11 sedentary controls) did two CPET sessions on consecutive days; blood drawn within 2 h before each test (day 1, day 2) and at home on day 3 and 7 (S2.4.p1, S2.5.p1). Day 1 is the unexercised baseline; day 2, 3, 7 are post-exercise samples. All 99 samples carry the exercise treatment field; the exercise factor is time relative to CPET, with disease as a second factor.
blind.B2: Table 3: ME/CFS vs controls at day 1/2/3/7 and all days (6 DEGs all days, 1 at day 7); pre- vs post-exercise change in ME/CFS compared with controls (0 DEGs, S3.3.p2); within each group day 1 vs day 2/3/7 (0 DEGs each); low-VO2 and test-retest ME/CFS subsets vs regular (subject labels not in GEO). n = 14 vs 11 subjects x 4 days (55 vs 44 samples in GEO; G12 day 7 absent); two samples of one subject (day 3 and 7) removed for low coverage (S3.3.p1).
blind.B3: Yes. Each subject contributes 4 samples (S2.5.p1). Key: characteristics_ch1.4.individual identifier (also in title prefix); packet A shows 25 keys, 99/99 samples linked, one per day level.
blind.B4: The paper does not say whether comparisons were fitted jointly or per pair; it describes only the Partek multimodel per-gene choice (AICc among normal/lognormal/NB/Poisson) in S2.5.1.p1 and reports each comparison as a separate row in Table 3.
blind.B5: S2.5.1.p1: 'fold change was > +/- 1.5, p-value < 0.05, and adjusted p-value (or false discovery rate, FDR) < 0.1%' (strict inequalities). Table 4 lists DEGs with FDR 0.02-0.10, so the text may mean 10%. Counts: Table 3 ME/CFS vs controls 0/0/0/1 for day 1/2/3/7, 6 all days; within-group day 1 vs day 2/3/7 all 0.

checks.evidence: Ran as an exercise (CPET) series; metadata field treatment=Cardiopulmonary exercise and day 1/2/3/7 match S2.5.p1; ownership check passed.

Day levels d1/d2/d3/d7 = 25/25/24/23 and CFS/HC = 53/44 after excluding GSM3664608 and GSM3664609 (P14 day 3/7), reproducing S3.3.p1; both exclusions named with reasons; G12 day 7 absence noted. Control is day 1 within the same subject group.
Contrasts are d2/d3/d7 (treatment) vs d1 (control) and CFS vs HC (HC reference), matching Table 3 orientation.

Mechanical flag unused_subject_like_column names characteristics_ch1.4.individual identifier, but it is aliased to derived column 'subject' and used as a fixed blocking term (~0 + C(day) + C(subject), rank 28, residual df 69) in the within-group day contrasts; paired_change_pairs.json exists for the change-from-day-1 comparisons; cross-sectional dz_d* fits need no pairing. The flag is a false positive.
Paper silent (B4). Per-stratum fits (CFS, HC) match the Table 3 lower block layout; joint model rejected with a stated reason (subject nested in disease).
No batch/lane column in GEO; paper reports no batch effect by PCA (S2.5.p1, S3.3.p1); all female so no sex term; recorded in covariance reasoning.

Deposited file is Cufflinks isoform FPKM (hg19), summed to genes via MyGene mapping (40184/43497 mapped) and analysed by limma on log2(FPKM+1); no counts exist. Deviation from the paper's hg38 Partek gene FPKM is recorded in paper_data_discrepancies.json.

Paper text: FC > 1.5, p < 0.05, FDR < 0.1% (S2.5.1.p1). Applied padj < 0.1 and |log2FC| > log2(1.5) with literal padj < 0.001 as audit; the 0.1 reading is supported by Table 4 FDRs up to 0.10 and the choice is recorded as a discrepancy. Raw p < 0.05 not encoded; reasoning that it is non-binding is sound. Counts are 0 under every table-variant rule except the day-7 case, so the open threshold question does not change the exercise conclusions.

HANDBACK pairs ours vs Table 3 rows for the same contrasts (all 0, day-7 1 vs 1) and states that the day-7 DEG is a different gene (HARS2 vs LINC01158) and that the all-days, low-VO2 and test-retest comparisons were not run.

Not run: low-VO2/test-retest subsets (per-subject labels not in GEO or paper tables; holds) and all-days CFS vs HC (needs a within-subject correlation term the runner cannot fit). The second is a tool limitation, not an absence in the data; a sample-level fit with duplicateCorrelation could be a sensitivity analysis.

human_items: Open policy: FDR written '<0.1%' vs Table 4 FDR up to 0.10; applied 0.1 with 0.001 audit, consistent with the skill's discrepancy rule.
Optional: all-days ME/CFS vs controls (paper 6 DEGs) could be added as a sensitivity analysis with a within-subject correlation model.
summary: 该案例设计与论文一致：以第1天为基线、第2/3/7天为运动后，在ME/CFS和对照组内分别用含受试者区块项的limma拟合，并排除了论文同样剔除的P14第3、7天样本。机器标记 unused_subject_like_column 为误报，因为受试者列已作为 subject 进入模型。阈值（FDR 0.1 与 0.001 审计）和未运行的比较均已如实记录，结果与论文表3的计数一致，整体通过。
